movement_source: row 'Net interest margin (%)', column Full Year Ended 30 Jun 25 -> column Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26
headline: CBA's Group net interest margin fell 3 bps to 2.05% in FY26 from 2.08% in FY25 (KPI table, cash basis; the margin row carries no statutory label). Net interest income rose $1,563m or 7% to $25,586m on average interest earning assets up $92bn or 8% to $1,246bn, so margin compression, not volume, was the drag. The results book's own FY25→FY26 walk (adopted framing, sum check passed): Liquids -3, Asset pricing -5, Funding costs 0, Portfolio mix +2, Basis risk 0, Capital, Replicating and Other +5, Treasury & Markets -2 = -3 bps. The bank qualifies: excluding growth in liquid assets, which have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income, NIM was stable. The ASX release corroborates (2.05%, 3bpts on FY25) and the FY25 book confirms the 2.08% endpoint. The presentation's 'underlying net interest margin' variant moved 2.04%→2.05% (+1 bp) — a different measure, context only. Half-on-half (2.06% vs 2.04%, +2 bps) is a different comparison and supplies no driver here.

drivers.columns: Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26 vs 30 Jun 25
drivers.narrative: Liquid asset average balances increased $15 billion or 9% to $187 billion. The bank qualifies: liquid assets 'have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income' and excluding their growth NIM was stable. The slide splits this drag into increase in liquid assets -3 and increase in institutional repos -1 (total -4).

drivers.columns: Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26 vs 30 Jun 25
drivers.narrative: Home lending pricing down 4 bps and business and institutional lending pricing down 1 bp, 'primarily reflecting the impact of competition'. The slide splits home -4 into home loan competition -3 and cash rate lag -1, plus Business & Insto. lending -1. Home loan average balances grew $32bn or 5% to $630bn.

drivers.columns: Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26 vs 30 Jun 25
drivers.narrative: Published zero bar: 'Funding costs: Flat.' The slide's FY walk also shows Funding costs 0 bps. The bank discloses no sub-parts or reason for the full-year funding-cost movement; the half-on-half narrative (a different comparison) cites rising interest rates partly offset by unfavourable deposit mix.

drivers.columns: Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26 vs 30 Jun 25
drivers.narrative: 'Favourable asset mix from strong growth in business lending and favourable funding mix from strong growth in deposits.' Business and corporate loan average balances rose $27bn or 10% to $299bn, outpacing home loans (+$32bn or 5%). Slide: 'Favourable asset mix and deposits growing faster than lending'.

drivers.columns: Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26 vs 30 Jun 25
drivers.narrative: Published zero bar: 'Basis risk: Flat.' The slide's FY walk carries no basis-risk bar, consistent with a nil contribution for the full year. No sub-parts or reason disclosed.

drivers.columns: Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26 vs 30 Jun 25
drivers.narrative: 'Driven by higher earnings on the replicating portfolio due to changes in portfolio rate and volume (up 4 basis points) and higher earnings on capital hedges (up 1 basis point).' Slide labels the bar 'Interest rate risk hedging +5' with 'Replicating portfolio +4'; ASX release cites the same supports.

drivers.columns: Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26 vs 30 Jun 25
drivers.narrative: 'Due to lower risk management income in Treasury and growth in reverse sale and repurchase agreement balances.' The ASX release likewise flags institutional reverse sale and repurchase agreements, with liquid assets, as having broadly neutral impacts on net interest income.

notable_items: No notable items are flagged on the NIM walk; the results book publishes no ex-notables variant of the Group margin row.
limitations: The footnote-4 definition of the presentation's 'underlying net interest margin' variant was not located in the corpus; per CBA's standard vocabulary it is NIM excluding liquids and pooled facilities, so its +1 bp move is reported as context only and supplies no driver.

The book's walk groups liquid assets and institutional repos into one 'Liquids' bar (-3 bps); the slide's split (liquid assets -3, institutional repos -1, total -4) differs by 1 bp — a grouping/rounding difference, recorded as a disagreement.

The book quantifies the funding-costs and basis-risk bars only as 'Flat'; the published zero bars are the bank's explicit statement of nil contribution, but no sub-drivers are disclosed for the full-year comparison.

The cash-rate-lag component (-1 bp inside asset pricing) is named only in the slide's annotation of the FY walk; the book's FY narrative attributes asset pricing 'primarily' to competition without quantifying the lag separately.

The Group NIM row carries no cash/statutory label; it is reported on the bank's primary (cash) basis per the KPI table footnote 'Presented on a cash basis unless stated otherwise'. No statutory NIM is published, so no dual-basis movement exists for this metric.
